reason: C19 matches Johannes Jacobus Erasmus exactly and is recorded in Somerset, the declared district.
Wentzel Christoffel is a normal spelling variant of Wensel Christoffel, and C04 is in Somerset. The senior and parentage notes introduce no known contradiction.
C02 matches Casper Labuschagne in Somerset, with the parenthetical Jeremias omitted. The senior designation is consistent with a man married in 1795.
No candidate has the name Roelof or a compatible rendering of Roelof Johannes. Johannes Andries in C02 has a different name combination, despite sharing Johannes and the district.
C08 matches Coenraad Marthinus Vermaak in Uitenhage, with only the normal Marthinus/Martinus spelling variation.
C01 is explicitly a widow's entry. Nothing identifies the widow as Anna Elizabeth Retief or otherwise establishes that this is a claim for Johannes Dewald(t) Hattingh.
The sole candidate is Frederik Roelof Janse van Rensburg, not Nicolaas Janse van Rensburg. The shared Janse and Albany district do not overcome the different given names.
The closest candidate, C03, is Martinus Jacobus rather than Marthinus Johannes and is recorded in Uitenhage rather than Somerset. No candidate supplies a sufficiently compatible name.

Johannes Lodewikus is a compatible form of Johannes Lodewyk and is the only close full-name match. Beaufort differs from the tentative Colesberg district, but the name match outweighs that discrepancy and the senior note creates no known contradiction.
C02 matches Hans Jurgen Steyn exactly; the Graaff-Reinet district differs, but there is no contradictory parentage evidence. Hermanus in Somerset is a clearly different given name.
